name: Nilgiri Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Foothill forest of southwestern peninsular india (mysore southward to kerala)
description: Entirely indigo-blue male is unique; Verditer Flycatcher is brighter blue and more elongated. Female Nilgiri is gray overall, though can sometimes show a bluish tinge in good lighting.

name: Common Shelduck
rangeDescription: Breeds western europe to east-central asia; winters to northern africa through southern asia
description: Distinctive, large, rather gooselike duck of coastal wetlands, tidal mudflats, and nearby grassy fields. Striking plumage often looks simply black-and-white; at close range, head is deep glossy green, broad breast band dark rusty.

name: White-shouldered Triller
rangeDescription: Eastern java, bali, sulawesi subregion, and lesser sundas
description: Slender inhabitant of open wooded areas in lowlands and foothills. Smartly-patterned black-and-white male can be difficult to distinguish from Sulawesi and Pied Trillers where ranges overlap, but note his extremely narrow white eyebrow and less extensive white on the wing.

name: Gray-crowned Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Pacific slope of mexico (southern sonora to central oaxaca)
description: The only species of overall green woodpecker in west Mexico; endemic. Favors tropical forests and shade-coffee plantations in foothills.

name: White-bellied Minivet
rangeDescription: Peninsular india (punjab and rajasthan to bihar and mysore)
description: A beautiful minivet inhabiting open, dry scrub and savanna with scattered acacia (Prosopis) growth. The male has a glossy black upper body, face, and neck.

name: Tacarcuna Wood-Quail
rangeDescription: Far eastern panama and adjacent northwestern colombia (chocó)
description: This rare chickenlike bird has an exceptionally small range on the border between Panama and Colombia. Found on the ground in mature forest from around 1,000–1,400 m.

name: Spot-breasted Scimitar-Babbler
rangeDescription: Assam south of the brahmaputra to western myanmar (chin hills)
description: Pale-eyed babbler with a decurved bill. Note rusty-orange face, white underparts, lightly spotted breast, and brown flanks.

name: Black-and-white Warbler
rangeDescription: Canada to gulf states; winters mexico to peru and west indies
description: Distinctive warbler with bold black-and-white stripes over entire body. Adult males have black throat and cheek; females and immatures have white throat and paler cheek.

name: Bornean Treepie
rangeDescription: Mountains of borneo
description: Long-tailed corvid of Borneo’s hilly and montane forests; the only treepie in its range. Note stout black bill, black wings with white patch, and warm buffy brown underparts and face.

name: Swahili Sparrow
rangeDescription: Southern kenya to western tanzania, malawi, and northwestern mozambique
description: A drab sparrow of East Africa, gray with brown wings and a bright rufous rump and shoulder. Generally common within its range in savanna, in cultivated areas, and around human habitation.

name: Slaty-backed Forest-Falcon
rangeDescription: Humid costa rica to bolivia and amazonian brazil
description: Forest-falcons are well-named raptors; they are found almost exclusively inside the forest. They are generally slender and long-tailed, with long legs.

name: Scintillant Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Humid montane forest of costa rica and western panama
description: Small hummingbird, unique orange throat distinguishes male from all other hummingbirds in limited range. Female less obvious; she has speckled throat, orangey flanks, and all-rufous tail with black band and buffy tips.

name: Spotted Crake
rangeDescription: Palearctic; winters mediterranean to southern africa and southeastern asia
description: Medium-sized crake with dense whitish spotting and speckling on the neck and breast. Also note greenish legs and short yellow bill with a reddish base.

name: Nihoa Finch
rangeDescription: Nihoa island (northwestern hawaiian islands)
description: A finch-billed Hawaiian honeycreeper endemic to the island of Nihoa; does not occur on the main Hawaiian Islands. Unlikely to be confused with any other species; the only other passerine bird on Nihoa is the Millerbird, which lacks the Nihoa Finch’s heavy bill.

name: Plain Swift
rangeDescription: Madeira and western canary islands; winters in northern africa
description: Medium-sized swift, very similar to Common Swift, but is noticeably paler, especially against a dark background. Wings are narrower and very pointed and the tail is longer and more deeply forked than Common or Pallid Swifts.

name: White-browed Nuthatch
rangeDescription: Montane forest of southwestern myanmar (mount victoria)
description: This exquisite nuthatch can only be found in a tiny portion of Myanmar’s southern Chin Hills. The gray-white-and-rust color scheme of this species is unmistakable.

name: White-breasted Robin
rangeDescription: Southwestern western australia (geraldton to esperance)
description: Small plump songbird found in heavy vegetation along creeks in southwestern Australia. White below, gray above, with darker gray wings.

name: Biak Hooded Pitta
rangeDescription: Biak (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea)
description: Beautiful leaf-green pitta of Biak Island, off northwestern New Guinea. Like the other “Hooded-type” pittas with which it was formerly grouped, this species has a black head, powder-blue shoulder patch, and red on the lower belly and undertail.

name: Philippine Jungle Crow
rangeDescription: Philippines
description: Large crow endemic to the Philippines; note its relatively long, daggerlike bill with curved top. Entirely black with some glossiness evident in good lighting.

name: Red-crested Turaco
rangeDescription: Locally in woodland and savanna of western angola
description: A long-tailed, bulky greenish turaco with a yellow bill, a red crest (sometimes tipped white) extending down the nape, and a whitish face. In flight, it explodes from the canopy, showing distinctive deep red panels in the wings.
